notes: Candidate order: release bodies py-1.43.0 .. py-2.0.0 (only the py-2.0.0 'Breaking changes' list yields candidates), then the 2.0 upgrade guide in heading order, then the removal table row by row.

Unit decisions: DataFrame/LazyFrame/Expr/Series methods of the same name, read_X/scan_X twins and sync/async twins form one item (as in the brief's explode example); differently named callables in one line are separate items; one guide heading or table row per item, several parameters of the same callable in that row/heading form one item.
Wildcard rows (read/scan_*(rechunk), sink_*(retries), write_*(retries), rolling_*(min_periods)) are one item each, with family members in api_names.
Migration-guide anchors cite the GitHub blob URL of docs/source/releases/upgrade/2.md (SOURCES.tsv lists the raw URL).
Rust-only behaviour changes with no Python-side trace were marked failed/cannot_locate per the brief.

candidates.description: SQL window functions in grouped queries now run over the aggregated rows and QUALIFY is evaluated before the projection.
candidates.source_quote: Run SQL window functions over grouped rows on the aggregated rows, and evaluate QUALIFY before the projection

candidates.description: SQL exact numeric literals become Decimal instead of Float64, and SQL %, MOD, DIV now truncate toward zero.
candidates.source_quote: Type exact SQL numeric literals as Decimal and truncate SQL `%`/DIV

candidates.description: Expression plugins are now treated as deterministic by default and may be deduplicated by common-subexpression elimination.
candidates.source_quote: Allow deterministic expression plugins to opt into CSE/CSPE

candidates.description: Parquet columns with the ENUM logical type are read as String instead of Binary.
candidates.source_quote: Read Parquet ENUM type as pl.String

candidates.description: engine='auto' in LazyFrame.collect now selects the streaming engine instead of the in-memory engine.
candidates.source_quote: `"auto"` now resolves to the streaming engine for lazy queries (it used to resolve to the in-memory engine)

candidates.description: pl.sql(eager=True) now collects through the default (streaming) engine instead of the in-memory engine.
candidates.source_quote: `SQLContext.execute(eager=True)` and `pl.sql(..., eager=True)` used to collect through the in-memory engine

candidates.description: SQLContext.execute(eager=True) now collects through the default (streaming) engine.
candidates.source_quote: `SQLContext.execute(eager=True)` and `pl.sql(..., eager=True)` used to collect through the in-memory engine

candidates.description: read_csv drops the n_threads, batch_size, sample_size and rechunk parameters.
candidates.source_quote: It loses `n_threads`, `batch_size`, `sample_size`, and `rechunk`, which have no equivalent in the lazy reader

candidates.description: read_csv now behaves like scan_csv: list schema_overrides must cover all columns and columns=[...] keeps requested order.
candidates.source_quote: a `schema_overrides` list must cover every column in the file, and `columns=[...]` returns columns in the requested order

candidates.description: read_ipc drops the memory_map and rechunk parameters.
show_graph plan_stage default changes from 'ir' to 'physical'.
candidates.source_quote: `LazyFrame.show_graph()`'s `plan_stage` parameter now defaults to `"physical"` instead of `"ir"`.

candidates.description: LazyFrame.profile is removed.
pl.concat(how='horizontal') now raises on unequal heights instead of null-padding; strict=False is rejected.
candidates.source_quote: `how="horizontal"` now always requires equal heights, matching what `strict=True` used to mean.

candidates.description: pl.union(how='horizontal') now requires equal heights instead of null-padding.
candidates.source_quote: `how="horizontal"` now always requires equal heights, matching what `strict=True` used to mean.

candidates.description: explode() empty_as_null now defaults to False, so empty lists produce no rows.
candidates.source_quote: An empty list now explodes into zero rows, rather than one `null` row.

candidates.description: is_in only coerces operands losslessly and raises otherwise.
candidates.source_quote: `is_in()` no longer lossily coerces operands to a shared supertype

candidates.description: Selector &, |, ^ with pl.col(...) is now an element-wise operator rather than a column set operation.
candidates.source_quote: Combining a selector with `pl.col(...)` via `&`, `|`, or `^` used to be special-cased

candidates.description: pl.datetime output column is named after its leftmost argument instead of 'datetime'.
candidates.source_quote: `pl.datetime(...)` and `pl.repeat(...)` used to always name their output column

candidates.description: pl.repeat output is named after its leftmost argument (or 'literal') instead of 'repeat'.
candidates.source_quote: `pl.datetime(...)` and `pl.repeat(...)` used to always name their output column

candidates.description: list/arr.to_struct turns a null row into a null struct rather than a struct of nulls.
candidates.source_quote: A `null` list or array row now converts to a `null` struct

candidates.description: Readers no longer seek file-like sources back to position 0 before reading.
candidates.source_quote: Reading from a file-like object (e.g. `io.BytesIO`) no longer implicitly rewinds it to the start.

candidates.description: Zero-width frames keep their height; pl.DataFrame() has fixed height 0.
candidates.source_quote: `DataFrame`/`LazyFrame` with zero columns now carry a height rather than collapsing to `(0, 0)`.

candidates.description: from_arrow on an object exposing only __arrow_c_stream__ returns a Series (of Struct) instead of a DataFrame.
candidates.source_quote: now always returns a `Series`, rather than a `DataFrame`

candidates.description: DataFrame.__dataframe__ (interchange protocol entry point) is removed.
The polars.interchange submodules and protocol symbols are removed; only CompatLevel remains.
from_dataframe no longer falls back to the interchange protocol; non-PyCapsule objects raise.
candidates.source_quote: `pl.from_dataframe()` is kept, but only accepts objects supporting the Arrow PyCapsule interface

candidates.description: from_dataframe drops the allow_copy parameter.
Transposing an empty DataFrame no longer raises.
candidates.source_quote: `DataFrame.transpose()` on a zero-height or zero-width `DataFrame` no longer raises

candidates.description: shift(n=None) now raises instead of warning and returning nulls.
candidates.source_quote: A `null` shift amount used to emit a `DeprecationWarning` and return a column of `null`s.

candidates.description: Unregistered Arrow extension types load as pl.Extension instead of their storage type.
candidates.source_quote: It now loads it as a generic `pl.Extension(name, storage)` dtype, and the warning is gone.

candidates.description: Arrow/Parquet/Iceberg map columns load as the new Map dtype instead of List(Struct).
candidates.source_quote: They now load as `Map`, and their Python values are `dict`s rather than lists of key/value structs.

candidates.description: round() on Decimal(p, s) now returns Decimal(p+1, s) where it can round up.
